configure_manager.title: Login to Meross Local Cloud
configure_manager.description:
**Broker detected automatically.**

Use the local account created in the Meross Local Broker add-on. Do not use your Meross cloud credentials; this integration only talks to the local broker.

If the add-on's exposed ports were changed (Settings → Apps → Meross Local Broker → Configuration), enter the address and ports manually.

Example: 192.168.1.10 — HTTPS 2004, MQTT 2001.

configure_manager_missing.title: Login to Meross Local Cloud
configure_manager_missing.description:
The broker was not detected automatically. Check that the Meross Local Broker add-on is installed and running: {broker_url}.

If the add-on's exposed ports were changed (Settings → Apps → Meross Local Broker → Configuration), enter the address and ports manually.

Example: 192.168.1.10 — HTTPS 2004, MQTT 2001.

configure_manager_reauth.title: Reauthentication required
configure_manager_reauth.description:
Existing broker configuration. Adjust the address or ports if needed.

Example: 192.168.1.10 — HTTPS 2004, MQTT 2001.

confirm.title: Remove the device?
confirm.description:
**{name}** (`{uuid}`) has not been reported by the broker for more than 48 hours. If it was unpaired or deleted on purpose, fix this issue to remove its device and entities from Home Assistant.

Delete **{name}** and its Home Assistant entities? Re-pairing the device later recreates them with the same identity.

unsupported_device.title: No device profile for {name}
unsupported_device.description: The broker reports **{name}** (`{uuid}`, type `{type}`), but no catalog profile matches it. Its entities are not created. Add or update the profile in the broker catalog; the integration reloads automatically when the revision changes.
